analysis: This batch contains only test changes. In CoordinatorIntegrationTests.swift, the head comments at lines 10-12 and 21 now say the suite runs in the provider CI lane (scripts/run-provider-tests.sh) rather than being skipped. The file adds tests 3c (head 456-472) and 3d (head 474-490). Test 3c expects a coordinator 1012 close to produce re-registration within 1.5s. Test 3d expects a session open past the stable duration to reset the backoff. New helpers are reregistrationTime (681-693) and withGrownReconnectBackoff (699-727). makeClient now passes reconnectPolicy to the CoordinatorClient initializer (653, 675). CoordinatorReconnectPolicyTests.swift is a new file whose head is not visible beyond its patch excerpt. That excerpt shows policy rows: the backoff resets after a session of at least 60s, a close with code 1012 gets a 0-1s wait without backoff growth, and other ends keep ExponentialBackoff(1,30) ranges. No production source is included in this batch, so these tests imply but do not show the production CoordinatorReconnectPolicy and its runLoop integration. Security-relevant question for integration (TB-002, availability): the 1012 fast-reconnect path is triggered by a close code the coordinator sends. The coordinator is trusted, but a network middlebox cannot forge WS close frames under TLS, so that path seems low-risk. Still, check that repeated 1012 closes cannot produce an unbounded tight reconnect loop, since the policy appears never to grow the backoff on 1012; the floor is 0-1s jitter. Also confirm that a reconnect still performs a full register and attestation, with no reuse of grant or authorization state across sockets (T-053, A-016). None of this is visible here. The test fixtures use fake signatures and mock keys only. No findings, because the changes are test-only and no production behavior is visible.
